title: Bernoulli's Principle: Venturi Fluid Dynamics & Energy Conservation
pedagogical_goal: Visually demonstrate that when an incompressible fluid flows through a constricted section of pipe, its velocity increases according to the continuity equation, while its internal static pressure simultaneously decreases according to Bernoulli's principle.

conservation_laws: Continuity Equation: A1 * v1 = A2 * v2 = Q (Volumetric Flow Rate)
Bernoulli Equation: P1 + 0.5 * rho * v1^2 = P2 + 0.5 * rho * v2^2 = Constant (assuming horizontal flow h1=h2)

components.description: Horizontal Venturi tube with 3 zones: Section 1 (wide inlet, x: 50-250), Converging Transition (x: 250-380), Section 2 Throat (narrow constriction, x: 380-520), Diverging Transition (x: 520-650), Section 3 Outlet (wide recovery, x: 650-850).
Transparent vertical tubes connected to the top of the pipe showing liquid height h = P / (rho * g). Column 2 drops dramatically compared to Column 1, demonstrating Bernoulli drop.

Particles flow continuously from left to right along streamline curves. In Section 1, particles move at speed v1. As they enter the throat, they accelerate to v2 and stretch/bunch closer vertically. In Section 3, they decelerate back to v1.
Interactive arrow overlays showing instantaneous velocity vectors. Arrow in Section 2 is visibly much longer than in Section 1 and Section 3.

Real-time energy bars at Section 1 vs Section 2 showing: [Static Pressure Energy P] + [Kinetic Energy 0.5*rho*v^2] = [Total Mechanical Energy]. Shows that total height is constant, but in Section 2 kinetic energy expands while static pressure shrinks.

lifecycle_rules: Use React useRef for DOM/SVG references
Use gsap.context() inside useEffect for proper cleanup on re-renders
Animate particles using GSAP timelines or ticker loops with ease: 'none' for smooth continuous fluid flow
Smoothly tween manometer liquid levels (height and y) using gsap.to() with duration: 0.6, ease: 'power2.out' when parameters change
Tween velocity arrow lengths and energy bar widths/heights smoothly on parameter adjustment

pedagogical_callouts.title: 1. The Narrower Path
pedagogical_callouts.text: Because fluid cannot be created or destroyed, the volume flowing in must equal the volume flowing out (A1·v1 = A2·v2). When the pipe narrows at the throat, fluid must speed up!

pedagogical_callouts.title: 2. Energy Conservation
pedagogical_callouts.text: As fluid accelerates into the throat, its Kinetic Energy (½ρv²) surges. By the Law of Conservation of Energy, that energy must come from somewhere—it is borrowed from the internal Static Pressure (P)!

pedagogical_callouts.title: 3. The Manometer Reading
pedagogical_callouts.text: Look at the vertical glass tubes: The liquid column above the constricted throat drops lower than the inlet! This physical drop proves the pressure in the fast-moving fluid has plummeted.

technical_requirements.styling: Tailwind CSS utility classes or modern inline styles with dark glassmorphism
technical_requirements.no_broken_dependencies: All icons or helper components should be pure SVG or standard HTML to ensure instant zero-error execution in any preview environment
